records.note: No deciding body and no countable set. 'Almost all psychiatric conditions' names no set of conditions, and 'first line' names no guideline, source or threshold. A horizon ('in 10 years' = 2033-04-10) exists, but no event can be written without inventing the guideline body and the share of conditions. The narrower companion claim on TMS in depression is the scorable one.

event.asset: Telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances: a permanent DEA rule
event.title: DEA adopts a permanent rule for telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances
event.proposition: The DEA adopts a permanent final rule for the prescribing of controlled substances by telemedicine without a prior in-person medical evaluation.
event.criterion: TRUE on the Federal Register publication date of a DEA final rule that sets a permanent framework for the prescribing of controlled substances by telemedicine without a prior in-person medical evaluation. A proposed rule, a temporary rule, and an extension of the COVID-era telemedicine flexibilities are not adoption. FALSE at the deadline when no such final rule has been published in the Federal Register. Resolution source: the Federal Register (DEA final rules).
readings: 'They' = the DEA, the only body in the immediate context on telehealth prescribing of controlled substances.
'Figure it out' = the DEA settles a permanent rule for telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances, per the immediate context.
A temporary rule or an extension of the COVID-era flexibilities is not the permanent rule the context names.
'Eventually' is not a deadline; the item goes to the undated panel.

records.stage_note: DEA rulemaking on telemedicine prescribing of controlled substances is open at the statement date. No class in base-rates.json covers adoption of a permanent telemedicine rule; the dea_telemedicine_extension class covers extensions of the flexibilities, which the criterion excludes.
records.note: The DEA is a third party and the context names one observable action: a permanent rule. 'They'll' is 'they will', so bin A. 'Eventually' sets no deadline, so the item goes to the undated panel.

The sentence bundles an open set: 'and other novel interventions'. 'Standard of care' names no deciding body, no guideline and no threshold, so no observable event can be written without invention. 'In the near future' is not a deadline. CONTROL was considered because the author's Acacia Clinics sells fMRI-guided TMS, but the field, not Acacia, would set a standard of care; the claim fails on vagueness first.

The headline claim is 'more effective treatment coming': the quantifier 'more' has no countable set. The four named candidates are each hedged ('like', 'probably', 'maybe even', 'may') and closed with 'I don't actually know', and each names no sponsor, trial, endpoint or authorization. A split gives only two records, so four candidates cannot be carried. 'Coming' and 'in the future' set no deadline.

The claim of this row is the private-equity call: 'Private Equity will see the goldmine in Accelerated TMS ... for dogs'. 'Private Equity' names no firm and no countable set, 'goldmine' is a slogan, and no threshold, deal count or data series is given. Veterinary use also sits outside the five areas. The United clause is the paired next sentence and is already carried on its own row (E-0040).

'Might work' is a bare efficacy word. The quote names no trial, no sponsor, no population, no endpoint and no source, so a trial_result event would have to be invented. The FDA-label clause is a statement of present fact, not an expectation. The paired sentence 'We should run to the studies' is normative.

A presupposition inside a clause about financials. 'The psychedelics and medical devices that are coming' names no compound, no sponsor, no regulator and no observable action. 'Are coming' sets no deadline. The direct restatement later in the post is the scorable row.

The main clause is retrospective: Spravato 'has already been approved a while ago'. The rest is an inference about feasibility, 'the challenges ... can be successfully overcome'. No future state is asserted and no deciding body or date is given. The forecast from this post, the 'strong chance that MDMA ... will get approved' line, is already in the ledger.

Two clauses describe facts: the re-domiciliation has happened, and it is 'a key prerequisite' for index inclusion. Neither says inclusion will happen, so E-0059 cannot be written without inventing the assertion. The one forward clause, '2026 will be a defining year for $ATAI', is a slogan with no observable event or threshold.

'FDA guidance has been consistent' describes published guidance at the statement date. The sentence reports the state of that guidance; it asserts no future FDA decision on any product, so E-0067 cannot be written from these words.

The approval claim is attributed: 'what the market anticipates will be the first regulatory approval'. The author asserts a change in public sentiment, not his own expectation of approval, and the confidence word belongs to the market. 'On the verge' sets no deadline. Near-identical text is already logged as angermayer-0161 from a later post.

'The REMS that we have proposed preliminary with the FDA is that ...' describes a proposal MAPS has already made. The tense is descriptive and no FDA action is asserted. The later Doblin lines that do assert the restriction in the future tense are the scorable ones (E-0077).

The forecast is that MAPS will know the MAPP1 result 'before the end of September', not that the endpoint is met, so E-0002 does not fit. Unblinding and analysis are internal actions of the sponsor, the forecaster's own organization, which sets the timing by its own decision. The '90% or greater probability of statistical significance' is the design power for 100 participants, which he says was not used; it is not a stated probability for the outcome.

'About a month away from having the data' is the timing of the sponsor's own internal readout, not a claim that the endpoint is met, so E-0002 does not fit. The forecaster's own organization, MAPS, controls when it holds the data. Same shape as doblin-0252.
